source: pinned OSHB Masoretic WLC and linked BDB/Strong

verses.english_main_research_candidate: And God — He said: Let a firmament be in the midst of the waters; and let [him] be separating between waters to waters.
And God — He made the firmament, and He separated between the waters which from beneath to the firmament, and between the waters which from above to the firmament; and so was.
And God — He called to the firmament Heavens; and was evening, and was morning: day second.
And God — He said: Let the waters from beneath the heavens be gathered unto place one, and let the dry ground be seen; and so was.
And God — He called to the dry ground Earth, and to the gathering of the waters He called Seas; and God — He saw that — good.

notes.text: Raqia is rendered firmament by OLT owner lock. BDB records extended surface; other source-compatible English alternatives are discussed in notes rather than substituted into the main text.
The first yehi is tagged Qal jussive. The following vihi is tagged Qal yiqtol (HC/Vqi3ms) in OSHB, and a volitive English rendering is proposed from context. Neither form is treated as wayyiqtol.
Mavdil is Hiphil masculine singular active participle (HVhrmsa), rendered separating; not English simple-past separated.
[him] in the proposed English phrase let [him] be separating is an English editorial completion referring to masculine firmament; no independently written Hebrew him occurs here.
Vayyaas is Qal wayyiqtol third-person masculine singular (OSHB HC/Vqw3ms). The OLT lexical lock requires made, never shaped.
The et token marks a direct object. Its English standalone lexical gloss is empty but the original token remains in the source alignment.
Vayehi (HC/Vqw3ms) is wayyiqtol and therefore must be simple past. The OLT research clause and so was preserves the past verb without an English neutral it.
Yom sheni uses the ordinal second, contrasting with Genesis 1:5 yom echad, the cardinal one. The intentionally awkward English day second preserves the source order.
Yiqqawu carries OSHB HVNj3mp (Niphal jussive 3mp). Let the waters be gathered is a volitive construction and is NOT a past-tense wayyiqtol.
Veteraeh is OSHB HC/VNi3fs (Niphal imperfect 3fs), not wayyiqtol. Let the dry ground be seen is a contextual proposal, not an assertion that the verb is morphologically jussive.
Miqveh here means gathering/collection of the waters. This must not be automatically conflated with other same-consonant terms or with later ritual mikveh solely from spelling.
The first called is OSHB wayyiqtol and the second qara (HVqp3ms) is qatal. Both can use English called but must not be classified as the same Hebrew verb form.
Ki tov is literally that good with a verbless adjective phrase. Do not mechanically assign the [he was] completion from Genesis 1:4 to a different subject without grammatical and contextual review.
